text: Before writing a named-account page, read two sections of `read_account_research`: **overview** and **insights** … They are enough for an account page.
note: Site: same two pages arrive as files.

text: Read **contacts** (the people on the buying committee) only when the page needs them: a page for one person, or a brief that asks you to speak to a specific role. … What you learn about people shapes the argument; never name them on an account page.
Separate source facts from analyst interpretations such as "needs a win", "empty evaluation slate" or "coverage gap". … a plausible sales angle is not evidence of need.
Identity alone supports a named concept. Supplied professional tasks plus seller proof support a task-relevant proposal. Account evidence can ground the argument; application remains proposed.

Write one compact chain in the plan: **reader/decision → selected account context and source/status → documented seller mechanism and source → proposed application → relevant proof/fit questions → genuine next action/destination**.
note: Overlaps site D1 message plan (Reader, Insight, Priorities, Offer and action, Proof).

text: Why this is relevant here → Account initiative or operating context … What the product changes → A proposed workflow with documented product actions, inputs and human handoffs … Why believe the proposal → Real product states, attributed customer evidence … What to evaluate next → The reader's criteria, dependencies to establish, fit questions and genuine next action
These are **content responsibilities, not mandatory sections or a fact quota**. Combine/expand them for the decision.
For each retained insight, record the visible explanation it enables and its section; give a reason for omitted material. Research only in the plan has not personalized the page.
Preserve the seller's geometry, type and imagery. Do not shrink copy into slogans.

loc: The shape of a 1:1 account page
text: Pick two or three priorities the research supports, each in the account's own words … Pair each with the seller capability that serves it, and say how it would apply here. This is a proposal, so it "would" help; it never "will". … Then attributed proof from similar customers … Then one action.
note: Same as site D1 1-Priorities and 5.2. Site D1 uses "could", not "would".

loc: The shape of a 1:1 account page
text: Swapping in the company's name and logo is not personalization. If the account has no research, say so in your handoff and write only what the seller's own facts support.

loc: The shape of a 1:1 account page
text: The brief's suggested structure is direction: follow it when it serves this shape, change it when a better order serves the reader.
note: duplicate of site A1 "The facts, proof and structure it suggests are suggestions."

text: "Imported materials name you", "not a biography" and "no claim of live deployment" are audit language. Replace them with the supported application and what the reader can assess.

loc: Review the page, not the plan
text: For every decision-map responsibility, point to the **actual visible explanation or working demonstration**. … Missing substance is a content defect even when many sections render cleanly.
